newsitem.title: GERMANY: Augsburg Airway international deal set for Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: Augsburg Airway international deal set for Oct 1.

text.p: German regional carrier Augsburg Airways said it has agreed a co-operation deal with an unnamed partner to fly international services out of Munich.
The airline said in an invitation to an October 1 news conference that it would start services from Munich to three domestic destinations.
The co-operation with the "strong partner" would be extended to exclusive international destinations next year, it added.
Augsburg Airways marketing manager Claus Fischer told Reuters the name of the partner and details of the co-operation could not be released before October 1.
The airline entered a co-operation with British Airways last year to fly from its home airport of Augsburg via Cologne to Birmingham and London City Airport.
Augsburg Airlines carried 105,400 passengers on its inner-German network in 1995 using a fleet of four Dash-8 turboprop aircraft.
